methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates scRNA-seq from 15 treatment-naive EGFR-mutant LUAD patients, matched patient-derived organoids (PDOs) with CAF coculture models, FACS-sorted RGS5+MYL9+ CAF subsets, LUAD cell lines (HCC827, PC9) with osimertinib-induced DTP models, FRET biosensors for ATP and RhoA activation, mitochondrial tracking dyes, GTP-RhoA pull-down, Miro1 shRNA knockdown, chemotaxis assays with CCL11 neutralizing antibody, cytokine arrays, ELISA, xenograft models with combination therapy arms (osimertinib + αCCL11 or osimertinib + fasudil), TCGA-LUAD CIBERSORTx deconvolution, and survival analysis. Statistical methods include Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and DESeq2 differential expression with adjusted P<0.05 threshold.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical study using cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and xenograft models - Oxford LoE 5. Translational relevance is exceptionally high because the proposed combination (osimertinib + FDA-approved Rho kinase inhibitor fasudil) is immediately clinically testable in EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients with MRD/DTP state, addressing a major unmet need in lung oncology. Fasudil is an established drug, substantially lowering barriers to clinical translation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed with RRID identifiers for cell lines, antibodies, software, and biosensors; ethics approval (Jiangsu Cancer Hospital No. 2020129) cited; animal protocols approved by Nanjing Medical University Animal Care Committee; dosing regimens clearly specified (osimertinib 5 mg/kg/day, fasudil 50 mg/kg 5x/week, αCCL11 5 mg/kg/week). Sample size justifications not explicitly reported. Data availability (scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq deposition) accession numbers not explicitly stated in the reviewed text.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies a previously unrecognized RGS5+MYL9+ CAF subpopulation in EGFR-mutant LUAD and reveals the counterintuitive mechanism of cancer-to-CAF (rather than CAF-to-cancer) transfer of damaged mitochondria via TNTs as a metabolic sink sustaining DTP cells. Mechanistic chain: TKI-induced mtROS -> Miro1/RhoA -> TNT formation -> CCL11 CAF recruitment -> damaged mitochondria offloading. The fasudil + osimertinib combination approach is novel and repurposes an established drug.

writing_presentation.justification: Abstract is duplicated (formatting artifact). Manuscript has clear logical flow from CAF identification (scRNA-seq) to functional characterization (mitochondrial transfer via TNTs) to therapeutic intervention (fasudil combination). Methods are appropriately detailed. Figures likely numerous with FRET imaging, flow cytometry, and xenograft data.

key_strengths: Discovery of RGS5+MYL9+ CAF subset via scRNA-seq of 15 patients with functional validation through FACS-sorted primary cells and matched PDOs
Novel direction of mitochondrial transfer (tumor-to-CAF) serving as metabolic sink for damaged mitochondria, mechanistically linking mtROS-Miro1-RhoA-TNT-CCL11 axis
Direct therapeutic demonstration: FDA-approved Rho kinase inhibitor fasudil combined with osimertinib in xenografts improves relapse-free and overall survival - a readily translatable combination
Multi-model validation across cell lines, PDOs, and xenografts with FRET biosensors for ATP and RhoA dynamics
key_concerns: Patient cohort (n=15) for scRNA-seq is modest; TCGA-LUAD deconvolution (CIBERSORTx) offers indirect rather than direct validation
Cell-line DTP models (HCC827, PC9) may not fully recapitulate clinical MRD heterogeneity
Data availability (RNA-seq accession numbers) not explicitly reported in reviewed text
Duplicated abstract suggests formatting/editorial issues requiring revision
Long-term safety of prolonged Rho kinase inhibition in combination not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically compelling preclinical study with novel CAF-tumor mitochondrial interaction and directly translatable fasudil combination strategy for EGFR-TKI resistance, fitting Tier 2 (Cancer Research / Clinical Cancer Research-caliber) with minor revisions.
